en: Udāna 2.3 Daṇḍasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a number of young boys were striking a snake with a stick between Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Grove.
Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.
The Blessed One saw many boys between Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Grove beating a snake with a stick.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the significance of this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
He who harms others with a rod,
does not obtain happiness after death.
He who, seeking his own happiness,
does not harm with a stick those beings who also desire happiness—
Having passed away, he obtains happiness. Thus ends the third [sutta].
